newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines edge up on active buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines edge up on active buying.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices edged higher on a revival in buying interest and slightly higher NYMEX prices, brokers said.
Buying increased ahead of Tuesday's afternoon's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute, which analysts forecast to show nationwide builds in gasoline stocks.
A lack of selling also aided the morning market, which saw slight gains in Los Angeles gasoline and CARB diesel prices.
San Francisco products shrugged off news of a weekend leak on Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline, which forced operators to shut part of the line between San Francisco and Reno, Nevada.
A state official said investigators are digging through snow to determine why diesel fuel is leaking from the line.
Meanwhile, NYMEX unleaded gasoline for April delivery rose 1.08 cents to 62.85 at 1137 PST.
In West Coast spot trade, a CARB gasoline cargo sold at 73.50 cents in L.A.. The grade was talked 73.50 to 74 cents, with bids a half-cent higher than yesterday's late levels.
L.A. conventional unleaded gasoline sold for 69.75 cents, with late morning bids seen at 69 cents and offers 70 cents.
CARB diesel in southern California was assessed 72/73, up 1.50 cents a gallon from Monday.
But offers for San Francisco material rose 0.50 cents to 71.50 cents, the only gains seen in Bay distillates despite the pipeline news.
